title: Perioperative Role Of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor In Cardiac Surgery-associated Acute Kidney Injury
official: Perioperative Role Of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor In Cardiac Surgery-associated Acute Kidney Injury
summary: The goal of this prospective observational study is to find out whether the protein vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) measured in blood and urine can predict which patients will develop acute kidney injury (AKI) after heart-type surgery that uses a heart-lung machine (cardiopulmonary bypass).
conditions: Cardiac Surgery Associated - Acute Kidney Injury
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Elective cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass
3. Written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Pre-existing chronic kidney disease with an eGFR \<20 ml/min/1,73m2
2. Usage of VEGF-inhibitors
3. Patients with pre-existing AKI within the last 30 days
4. Patients undergoing one of the following surgeries:

   1. Emergency surgery
   2. LVAD-implantation
5. Patients after cardiac arrest requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation within the last 6 months
6. Patients on vasopressors, inotropes or mechanical circulatory support before surgery
